---
title: Scanners
llms-description: "How Steward scans transcripts for scoring integrity problems: the built-in scanner, choosing a scan model, adding your own, and what a finding asks of you."
---

## Overview

A sample can run, score cleanly, and still be untrustworthy: the model read the grader, refused the task while producing something that looks like an answer, or retrieved remote data from inside a sandbox that should have had no route to the internet.

Scanners review transcripts for these problems. Under Steward they run as the samples they review complete, so the transcripts are already scanned by the time the run finishes.

Steward runs a scoring integrity scanner over every sample of every run. It requires no configuration, and can be [turned off](#turning-off-the-built-in-scanner).

## Scan Model

By default a scanner reviews with the model already under evaluation, so an unconfigured run still scans. To use a different model, set `scan_model` in `_steward.yaml` or `STEWARD_SCAN_MODEL` in your `.env`:

```{.ini filename=".env"}
STEWARD_SCAN_MODEL=anthropic/claude-opus-5
```

A scanner that names its own model in the definition keeps it.

## Adding Scanners

Your definition is the normal place to say what scans your eval set:

```{.python filename="evalset.py"}
eval_set(
    tasks=[cais_swebenchpro(), datacurve_deep_swe()],
    model=["openai/gpt-5.6-sol", "anthropic/claude-opus-5"],
    scanner=[my_scanner()],
)
```

## Disabling the Scanner

To run without the built-in scanner, set `integrity_scanner` in `_steward.yaml` or `STEWARD_INTEGRITY_SCANNER` in your `.env`:

```{.yaml filename="_steward.yaml"}
integrity_scanner: false
```

Scanners declared in your definition and in `scanners` still run. With nothing left, the run scans nothing.

Like any change of scanners, this takes effect at launch and is checked against what the run has already recorded: turning the built-in off on a run where it has already reviewed samples is refused.

## Findings

A flagged sample becomes an anomaly and is decided the same way an error is, as described in [Error Handling](errors.qmd). Samples flagged the same way in the same task are one class and one decision.

When the task's scan lands, the agent investigates each finding. The scanner over-flags by design, so each hit is a lead that the agent confirms or dismisses by reading the transcript. A finding ruled on one task is shown as precedent when another task lands with the same one.

Findings rooted in how the benchmark was built (a grader loophole, a tamperable grader, a scorer false positive) are kept scored as recorded. These faults recur on every run of the same dataset, so excluding or zeroing the samples would produce a number no other run has. Your agent rules them `score` itself after confirming the mechanism in the transcript. The finding is carried as a caveat in `anomalies.md`, written up in `analysis.md`. Findings that change no score (a refusal, a failed attempt to read the grader, a grader that could not grade its samples) are recorded the same way.

What reaches you for rulings are things that might be remedied by a re-run: a transient fault to run again, a successful sandbox escape or returned egress response to score zero, or genuine model misconduct. These arrive one row per class with a proposed disposition, your answers are recorded row by row, and the task's finished notification goes out with the proposals.

A run cannot be signed off while a finding has no ruling. At signoff Steward tells you how many findings were dismissed and how many were scored as recorded.
